readerContract.humanQuestion: What does a ChatGPT pet actually do, and can it help me personally or is it only a decorative avatar?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Tell a desktop reader which useful controls sit with a pet, what Mini does without an animal, and what a pet does not change.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: No knowledge of desktop apps, projects, Appshots, or ChatGPT task states is assumed.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: A pet is the optional appearance around a desktop quick-chat and activity-control surface; the controls can be useful, but the pet does not improve the chat itself.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: A person writing a birthday note or planning a dinner can start a small desktop chat while another app stays open, then choose whether a pet adds anything she wants.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A short dated reader explainer of OpenAI's September 11 desktop quick-chat update, not a performance review or a promise of automation.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I know whether I want the desktop controls, the pet, or Mini, and I know the one limit to check before I use them.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: A ChatGPT pet is optional desktop appearance around quick-chat and activity controls. It can make those controls easier to notice while you work, but it does not make answers better; Mini gives the same controls without an animal.
causalSequence: OpenAI dated the desktop quick-chat update September 11.
On macOS and Windows the floating controls can start a typed or voice chat and show whether a thread is working, needs input, is ready, or is blocked.
A pet changes the appearance around those controls, while Mini keeps the controls without a pet.
A quick chat begins outside a project, so a reader who needs project context must start inside that project in the main app.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: While planning a birthday dinner in another app, a reader can use the desktop controls to start a short ChatGPT chat and later open the thread when it needs her input.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: If the same reader needs a chat to use a project’s saved context, she starts it from that project in the main app instead of from the floating controls.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: On desktop, choose a pet if you want the companion visible or Mini if you want only the controls; use the main app for a project-aware chat.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: The Story; The LAiDIES Read; What This Means for You; Cocktail Party; Class Notes; Sources.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: Do not turn a cosmetic setting into an AI capability story. Answer the decoration question early, then teach the single controls-versus-context distinction.
